Railway Friction Wedge

Friction wedge inquiries for freight bogie suspension systems, specified against the approved wedge, bolster pocket and side-frame interfaces.

Product overview

A railway friction wedge is a suspension component used in certain freight bogie designs. Its interfaces operate with adjoining components such as the bolster pocket and side-frame friction surface. This is a different part from a tread brake shoe: a wedge belongs to the suspension arrangement, while a brake shoe acts within the braking system. Product naming should therefore be checked against the assembly drawing.

Application and configuration

Identify the bogie model, wedge part number, drawing revision and mating wear components. Specify whether the design uses a one-piece metal wedge, split configuration or separately approved facing. Geometry, material and surface condition form a system requirement. A change to one component should not be assumed compatible with the existing bogie merely because it fits the available space.

Technical information for quotation

Project-specific information to confirm
SystemBogie model, wedge position and mating assembly drawings
GeometryInclined face, contact surfaces, pocket fit and locating details
ConstructionSolid, split or faced design as specified
MaterialApproved grade and any facing or wear-surface requirement
InspectionCritical profiles, surface condition, identification and test scope

Manufacturing and supply review

The quotation should identify the blank and finishing route, material control and any specified heat or surface treatment. Where a separate facing is part of the design, confirm its attachment method and approval evidence. Do not infer a proprietary manufacturer's design or interchangeability from a generic product description. Any proposed alternative must be declared and reviewed.

Inspection and documentation

Check the drawing-defined contact profiles and dimensions using the agreed measurement method. Define permissible surface defects and the reporting requirements before production. System performance and service acceptance depend on the complete suspension arrangement; a component dimensional report does not replace the validation required by the vehicle authority.

Packaging and shipment

Keep contact faces protected from corrosion and mechanical damage. Segregate different drawing revisions and material variants, provide durable package identification and agree preservation for the shipping and storage period.

Request a technical quotation

Send the controlled drawing and revision, vehicle or bogie application, quantity, exact standards and editions, acceptance plan, required documents, packing requirements and destination. Frequently asked questions

Is a friction wedge a brake block?

No. The wedge is a suspension component; a brake block or brake shoe is part of the braking system. Supply the part drawing to avoid confusion.

Are all freight bogie wedges interchangeable?

No. Wedge geometry, construction and mating components depend on the approved bogie design. Any substitution requires authorized engineering review.

Can the drawing specify a faced wedge?

Yes, the inquiry can define a faced configuration, but the material, attachment, acceptance requirements and supply feasibility must be confirmed.
